findings.body: The victim's callback accepts the attacker's code because the state value is not bound to the victim's OAuth initiation, enabling login CSRF and cross-session substitution of the authenticated GitHub user.
findings.failure_mode: Callbacks carrying a publicly learnable state value are accepted by any active GitHub pipeline with the same provider signature.
findings.impact: The victim's callback accepts the attacker's code because the state value is not bound to the victim's OAuth initiation, enabling login CSRF and cross-session substitution of the authenticated GitHub user.
findings.root_cause: The patch reuses a deterministic pipeline-version signature as the OAuth CSRF token instead of generating session-specific state.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a cryptographically random nonce for each authorization attempt, bind it in pipeline state, and compare the callback value against that stored nonce before exchanging the code; consume the nonce after successful validation.
findings.title: OAuth state is a shared pipeline signature rather than a per-flow nonce
findings.trigger: An attacker obtains an OAuth code for their GitHub account and sends a callback URL to a victim who has an active GitHub integration pipeline. The pipeline signature is a deterministic signature of the provider's step configuration and is the same across installation sessions.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 402 shows `state = pipeline.signature` verbatim. The patch uses a deterministic pipeline signature as OAuth state instead of a per-session random nonce. This is a real CSRF weakness: the signature is derived from provider configuration and is identical across sessions, allowing an attacker who knows the signature to craft a callback URL that a victim's active pipeline will accept.

pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: The callback URI is built on the system URL prefix, but this view never binds `request.subdomain`. Consequently `PipelineAdvancerView` cannot redirect the callback back to the originating customer domain, and subsequent organization detection and installation checks run on the default host instead.
raw_findings.failure_mode: OAuth returns to and continues on the wrong host for customer-domain installations.
raw_findings.impact: The callback URI is built on the system URL prefix, but this view never binds `request.subdomain`. validated_findings.trigger: GitHub redirects the browser with an installation ID before the asynchronous installation webhook has created the corresponding Integration row.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that the DoesNotExist branch at line 482 advances without the installer check is incorrect. Line 482 shows `return pipeline.next_step()` only when Integration.DoesNotExist is raised (no integration exists yet). The installer validation at lines 501-505 applies when an Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration does. The patch logic is: no Integration → advance (nothing to validate against); Integration exists without OrgIntegration → validate sender. This is intentional design, not a bypass.

validated_findings.body: The callback replaces the installation selected when the pipeline started, so subsequent steps validate and attach B rather than A. It also mutates pipeline state even before an invalid callback state is rejected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A tampered callback changes which GitHub installation the pipeline processes.
validated_findings.impact: The callback replaces the installation selected when the pipeline started, so subsequent steps validate and attach B rather than A. It also mutates pipeline state even before an invalid callback state is rejected.
validated_findings.root_cause: Untrusted callback query data is persisted on every dispatch before the code distinguishes an initial request from an OAuth callback or validates state.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only bind `installation_id` on the initial request before redirecting to GitHub. On callbacks, ignore the query parameter or reject it when it differs from the already-bound value, and validate state before mutating any pipeline state.
validated_findings.title: OAuth callbacks can overwrite the installation ID before state validation
validated_findings.trigger: A direct-install pipeline already contains installation ID A, and the OAuth callback is supplied with a valid state plus a different `installation_id=B` query parameter.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 397-399 show `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id")` followed by `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)` before state validation at line 412. An attacker could supply a different installation_id in the callback, overwriting the bound value before state is checked. While state validation occurs afterward, the installation_id is already mutated in pipeline state.

validated_findings.body: The callback URI is built on the system URL prefix, but this view never binds `request.subdomain`. Consequently `PipelineAdvancerView` cannot redirect the callback back to the originating customer domain, and subsequent organization detection and installation checks run on the default host instead.
validated_findings.failure_mode: OAuth returns to and continues on the wrong host for customer-domain installations.
validated_findings.impact: The callback URI is built on the system URL prefix, but this view never binds `request.subdomain`. Consequently `PipelineAdvancerView` cannot redirect the callback back to the originating customer domain, and subsequent organization detection and installation checks run on the default host instead.
validated_findings.root_cause: The custom OAuth login implementation omitted the subdomain-preservation step required by the pipeline callback handler.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Before redirecting, bind `request.subdomain` into pipeline state when present, matching the behavior of the generic `OAuth2LoginView`.
validated_findings.title: Customer-domain origin is not preserved across the OAuth redirect
validated_findings.trigger: A GitHub installation is initiated from a request with an organization customer subdomain.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about subdomain preservation is speculative. The patch shows `self.determine_active_organization(request)` is called at line 391, and the standard OAuth2LoginView binds subdomain at line 253-254 in identity/oauth2.py. However, there's no evidence this specific view requires subdomain binding for correct operation, and PipelineAdvancerView handles subdomain redirection independently at lines 54-61. The impact is not proven from available evidence.

validated_findings.body: The authorization code exchange is rejected, so otherwise valid GitHub installations display the invalid-request error instead of completing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The token request is not protocol-compatible with servers that validate redirect URI binding.
validated_findings.impact: The authorization code exchange is rejected, so otherwise valid GitHub installations display the invalid-request error instead of completing.
validated_findings.root_cause: The hand-written token parameters omit fields supplied by the repository's standard OAuth callback implementation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Include the same computed `redirect_uri` in the token request, and include `grant_type=authorization_code` as done by the shared `OAuth2CallbackView`.
validated_findings.title: Token exchange omits the redirect URI used in the authorization request
validated_findings.trigger: GitHub or an OAuth-compatible deployment enforces OAuth 2.0's requirement that a token request repeat the identical `redirect_uri` when one was included in the authorization request.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 416-420 show the token request data omits `redirect_uri` and `grant_type`. The standard OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params at lines 273-280 includes both. OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749 section 4.1.3 requires redirect_uri in token request if it was included in authorization request. Line 408 shows redirect_uri was included in the authorization URL, so its omission in token exchange may cause rejection by strict OAuth servers.

validated_findings.body: The exception is outside the parsing try block and produces an unhandled 500 response rather than the integration failure page introduced by this patch.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Transient GitHub connectivity failures crash the installation endpoint.
validated_findings.impact: The exception is outside the parsing try block and produces an unhandled 500 response rather than the integration failure page introduced by this patch.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only response decoding is guarded; the external request that can raise is executed before the try block.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the token request itself in targeted request-exception handling, log the failure without credentials, and return the standard installation error response.
validated_findings.title: Token-endpoint connection failures escape as server errors
validated_findings.trigger: The GitHub token endpoint times out, has a DNS or TLS failure, or otherwise causes `safe_urlopen` to raise a requests exception.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 423 shows `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is called before the try block at line 425. The try block only wraps `safe_urlread(req).decode()` and `parse_qsl()`. If safe_urlopen raises a network exception (timeout, connection error), it will propagate as an unhandled 500 error rather than returning the error page. Compare to OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token at lines 282-308 which catches SSLError and ConnectionError.

validated_findings.body: `get_user_info` raises from `raise_for_status`, JSON decoding, or the network request, resulting in a 500 instead of the intended invalid-installation response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: OAuth installations crash whenever GitHub cannot return a valid user document.
validated_findings.impact: `get_user_info` raises from `raise_for_status`, JSON decoding, or the network request, resulting in a 500 instead of the intended invalid-installation response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new external user-information request has no exception boundary.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Catch the expected HTTP, connection, and decoding exceptions around `get_user_info`, log a sanitized diagnostic, and return the standard error page.
validated_findings.title: GitHub user lookup failures are not converted to installation errors
validated_findings.trigger: GitHub returns 401, 403, 429, 5xx, malformed JSON, or a network error from the `/user` endpoint after a token has been exchanged.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 434 shows `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` outside any try block. The get_user_info function at identity/github/provider.py:7-17 calls `resp.raise_for_status()` and `resp.json()`, both of which can raise exceptions. These would propagate as 500 errors rather than the intended error page shown at line 436.

validated_findings.body: The same GitHub account is treated as a different user and a legitimate integration installation is rejected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Identity equality changes when a user renames their account despite the underlying GitHub principal remaining unchanged.
validated_findings.impact: The same GitHub account is treated as a different user and a legitimate integration installation is rejected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch chooses a mutable, case-sensitive display identifier even though both GitHub responses provide an immutable numeric user ID.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Require and bind `authenticated_user_info["id"]`, then compare it with `integration.metadata["sender"]["id"]`; retain login only for display or diagnostics.
validated_findings.title: Installer comparison uses GitHub's mutable login instead of its immutable user ID
validated_findings.trigger: The installing GitHub user renames or changes the capitalization of their login between the installation webhook and the OAuth `/user` lookup, or an older pending installation contains the prior login.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 438 binds `authenticated_user_info["login"]` and line 503 compares against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. GitHub login is mutable (users can rename accounts) while user ID is immutable. Both responses include `id` field. If a user renames their GitHub account between webhook and OAuth callback, the comparison will fail despite being the same user.

validated_findings.body: Accessing `sender` or `login` raises `KeyError`, returning a 500 instead of safely rejecting or retrying the unverifiable installation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Legacy or partially created integration records crash the installation flow.
validated_findings.impact: Accessing `sender` or `login` raises `KeyError`, returning a 500 instead of safely rejecting or retrying the unverifiable installation.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new validation assumes every existing Integration has a complete webhook-derived `sender` mapping, despite other repository code explicitly handling its absence.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Read sender metadata defensively and return the standard retryable verification error when either the sender or immutable sender ID is absent; do not advance without verified metadata.
validated_findings.title: Missing sender metadata causes an unhandled KeyError
validated_findings.trigger: An active, unassociated GitHub Integration was created before sender metadata was persisted, by a webhook race, or by a partially completed legacy installation.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 503 accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without defensive checks. The installation.py file at line 44 shows `if "sender" not in integration.metadata:` indicating sender may be absent. Legacy integrations or race conditions could result in missing sender metadata, causing KeyError and 500 response instead of graceful error handling.

validated_findings.body: The installer validation reads the unrelated integration's metadata, causing an erroneous mismatch response or a KeyError and preventing a valid GitHub installation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cross-provider identifier collisions select the wrong database record for security validation.
validated_findings.impact: The installer validation reads the unrelated integration's metadata, causing an erroneous mismatch response or a KeyError and preventing a valid GitHub installation.
validated_findings.root_cause: The added lookup treats `external_id` as globally unique even though integrations are identified by provider plus external ID.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key` to this lookup and consistently scope the preceding existence query to the same provider.
validated_findings.title: The new Integration lookup is not scoped to the GitHub provider
validated_findings.trigger: An active, unassociated integration from another provider has the same opaque external ID as the GitHub installation being set up.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 494-496 show `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` without filtering by provider. The ensure_integration function at pipeline.py:38-39 uses both provider and external_id. If another provider has the same external_id, the wrong integration's metadata would be used for validation, causing incorrect behavior.
